# The radiative-transfer problem and its approximations {#sec-ch02}

This chapter sets up the radiative-transfer problem that both pyharp solvers approximate, and fixes the symbols the
solver chapters use. The atmosphere is a stack of homogeneous plane-parallel layers, each with optical thickness
$\Delta\tau$, single-scattering albedo $\omega$ and asymmetry parameter $g$, lit by a collimated beam and, in the
infrared, by its own Planck emission. The two-stream approximation keeps only two hemispheric fluxes. The sections
show that every named closure is one choice of four coefficients and which one each Toon path uses; how the forward
peak of a phase function is removed first; and the energy identities, with the failure of the closed-form solution
at $\omega = 1$. Every equation is checked by a script under `derivation-checks/`. The heating rate and the flux
output conventions are not provided here: they belong to the Radiation API chapter, not written yet.

The dependency map of the schemes is not provided: its figure module is not written yet.

| scheme | YAML key or option | default | order | main test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| @sec-ch02-closures | `flags: planck` (Toon) | shortwave, quadrature | exact algebra | `check_ch02_closures.py` |
| @sec-ch02-delta-scaling | `delta_eddington_lw` (Toon) | shortwave on, longwave off | exact algebra | `check_ch02_delta_scaling.py` |
| @sec-ch02-conservation | always; clamp in `RadiationBand` | clamp on | exact identities | `check_ch02_conservation.py` |
